answer.rationale: P99 latency climbing 5x during settlement peak with heavy writes rules out rollback (security patch cannot revert) and regional failover (introduces switchover latency when sustained throughput is the issue). memory_b5 demonstrates that routing read-heavy queries to replicas relieved primary load and recovered transactional write latency same-day without customer impact. memory_b3 shows capacity planning prevented queue buildup during peaks. Current situation has settlement traffic at daily peak with write pressure—routing dashboard/report queries off primary will reduce contention on the write path immediately. This is narrower scope than full capacity addition, preserves the security patch, and has proven precedent. Verification of memory_b5 will confirm the read-replica routing technique and latency recovery pattern applies here. If routing does not stabilize p99 within 20min, capacity addition becomes the next intervention.
